questions.stem: What does Fabric mirroring do with a supported operational database?

options.text: It moves the database into a Fabric warehouse and shuts down the source
It makes a one-time backup of the database in OneLake
It caches query results from the source in Power BI
It keeps a near real-time replica of the database's tables in OneLake as Delta tables

questions.explanation: Mirroring continuously replicates the source's data into OneLake in Delta format, so it can be analyzed in Fabric without building ETL pipelines.

questions.stem: Which three sources can Fabric mirroring replicate? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Azure Cosmos DB
Snowflake
Azure SQL Database
A CSV file share
A Power BI semantic model

questions.explanation: Azure SQL Database, Snowflake and Azure Cosmos DB are among the databases mirroring supports. File shares and semantic models aren't mirroring sources.

questions.stem: After a database is mirrored into Fabric, how can analysts query the replica with T-SQL?

options.text: Only by connecting to the source database
Only through KQL
Through the mirrored database's SQL analytics endpoint
They can't; the replica is visible only to Spark

questions.explanation: A mirrored database comes with a SQL analytics endpoint for read-only T-SQL queries over the replicated tables.

questions.stem: You need a continuously updated copy of an Azure SQL database in OneLake, with as little to build and maintain as possible and no transformation on the way. What should you use?

options.text: A Dataflow Gen2
A pipeline with a Copy activity scheduled every five minutes
Mirroring
A Spark notebook polling the source

questions.explanation: Mirroring is set up once and keeps the replica current with no pipelines or schedules to maintain. Pipelines and notebooks suit loads that need transformation or a source mirroring doesn't support.

questions.stem: Your organization has an F64 capacity and plans to mirror several operational databases. How much OneLake storage for the mirrored replicas is free?

options.text: 1 TB per mirrored database, whatever the capacity size
None; mirrored storage is billed at regular OneLake rates
64 TB, one free terabyte per capacity unit, used only for mirroring
64 GB, one free gigabyte per capacity unit, shared with all items

questions.explanation: Mirroring gives one free terabyte of mirroring storage per capacity unit, so F64 gets 64 TB that's only for mirroring.

questions.stem: A finance team asks how mirroring an Azure SQL database affects their Fabric capacity. Which two statements are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: The background compute that replicates data into OneLake is free and doesn't consume capacity
Replication compute is charged per changed row against the capacity
Mirroring needs a dedicated capacity separate from other workloads
Queries on mirrored data are free because the replica is read-only
Queries on the mirrored data from SQL, Power BI or Spark are charged at regular rates

questions.explanation: Replication compute is free, but querying the data with SQL, Power BI or Spark uses capacity at regular rates.

questions.stem: You set up mirroring for an Azure Databricks catalog in Fabric. How does the data become available?

options.text: Fabric imports the tables into a semantic model on a refresh schedule
Fabric syncs catalog metadata and uses OneLake shortcuts, so the data stays in its source
Fabric creates a pipeline that copies changed files every 15 minutes
Fabric copies every table into OneLake as Delta and keeps it in sync with CDC

questions.explanation: Azure Databricks uses metadata mirroring, which syncs catalog names, schemas and tables and references the data through shortcuts instead of copying it.

questions.stem: An in-house application stores data in a database that Fabric mirroring doesn't support natively. The team wants to push the application's change data into a mirrored database item. What should they use?

options.text: A Copy job that writes into the mirrored database's tables
Database mirroring by choosing the closest supported source type
Open mirroring, writing change data through its public APIs
Metadata mirroring with a shortcut to the database files

questions.explanation: Open mirroring lets any developer write an application's change data directly into a mirrored database item through public APIs, based on the Delta Lake format.

questions.stem: A mirrored database named CrmMirror contains the table dbo.Accounts. From a warehouse in the same workspace, which query joins it with dbo.Sales?

options.text: `SELECT * FROM dbo.Sales s JOIN CrmMirror.dbo.Accounts a ON s.AccountId = a.AccountId`
`SELECT * FROM dbo.Sales s JOIN external_table('CrmMirror.Accounts') a ON s.AccountId = a.AccountId`
`SELECT * FROM dbo.Sales s JOIN OPENROWSET('CrmMirror', 'dbo.Accounts') a ON s.AccountId = a.AccountId`
`SELECT * FROM dbo.Sales s JOIN [CrmMirror].[Accounts] a ON s.AccountId = a.AccountId`

questions.explanation: Cross-database queries use three-part names whose first part is the mirrored database name. The other forms aren't T-SQL cross-database syntax in Fabric.

questions.stem: Report authors want near real-time Power BI reports on a mirrored database without scheduling imports. Why can they do this?

options.text: Mirroring creates an import-mode semantic model that refreshes every 15 seconds
Mirroring sends each change to Power BI as a push dataset
Power BI queries the source database directly through the mirrored item
Mirrored data is stored in Delta Lake format in OneLake, which Power BI can read in Direct Lake mode

questions.explanation: Mirrored data lands in OneLake in Delta Lake format, so Power BI connects in Direct Lake mode and reads the files directly.
